NKJV.1: Job further continued his discourse, and said:
NKJV.2: “Oh, that I were as in months past, As in the days when God watched over me;
NKJV.3: When His lamp shone upon my head, And when by His light I walked through darkness;
NKJV.4: Just as I was in the days of my prime, When the friendly counsel of God was over my tent;
NKJV.5: When the Almighty was yet with me, When my children were around me;
NKJV.6: When my steps were bathed with cream, And the rock poured out rivers of oil for me!
NKJV.7: “When I went out to the gate by the city, When I took my seat in the open square,
NKJV.8: The young men saw me and hid, And the aged arose and stood;
NKJV.9: The princes refrained from talking, And put their hand on their mouth;
NKJV.10: The voice of nobles was hushed, And their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
NKJV.11: When the ear heard, then it blessed me, And when the eye saw, then it approved me;
NKJV.12: Because I delivered the poor who cried out, The fatherless and the one who had no helper.
NKJV.13: The blessing of a perishing man came upon me, And I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
NKJV.14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; My justice was like a robe and a turban.
NKJV.15: I was eyes to the blind, And I was feet to the lame.
NKJV.16: I was a father to the poor, And I searched out the case that I did not know.
NKJV.17: I broke the fangs of the wicked, And plucked the victim from his teeth.
NKJV.18: “Then I said, ‘I shall die in my nest, And multiply my days as the sand.
NKJV.19: My root is spread out to the waters, And the dew lies all night on my branch.
NKJV.20: My glory is fresh within me, And my bow is renewed in my hand.’
NKJV.21: “Men listened to me and waited, And kept silence for my counsel.
NKJV.22: After my words they did not speak again, And my speech settled on them as dew.
NKJV.23: They waited for me as for the rain, And they opened their mouth wide as for the spring rain.
NKJV.24: If I mocked at them, they did not believe it, And the light of my countenance they did not cast down.
NKJV.25: I chose the way for them, and sat as chief; So I dwelt as a king in the army, As one who comforts mourners.

ESV.1: And Job again took up his discourse, and said:
ESV.2: “Oh, that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me,
ESV.3: when his lamp shone upon my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,
ESV.4: as I was in my prime,  when the friendship of God was upon my tent,
ESV.5: when the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were all around me,
ESV.6: when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
ESV.7: When I went out to the gate of the city, when I prepared my seat in the square,
ESV.8: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the aged rose and stood;
ESV.9: the princes refrained from talking and laid their hand on their mouth;
ESV.10: the voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
ESV.11: When the ear heard, it called me blessed, and when the eye saw, it approved,
ESV.12: because I delivered the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had none to help him.
ESV.13: The blessing of him who was about to perish came upon me, and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.
ESV.14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.
ESV.15: I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
ESV.16: I was a father to the needy, and I searched out the cause of him whom I did not know.
ESV.17: I broke the fangs of the unrighteous and made him drop his prey from his teeth.
ESV.18: Then I thought, ‘I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand,
ESV.19: my roots spread out to the waters, with the dew all night on my branches,
ESV.20: my glory fresh with me, and my bow ever new in my hand.’
ESV.21: “Men listened to me and waited and kept silence for my counsel.
ESV.22: After I spoke they did not speak again, and my word dropped upon them.
ESV.23: They waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouths as for the spring rain.
ESV.24: I smiled on them when they had no confidence, and the light of my face they did not cast down.
ESV.25: I chose their way and sat as chief, and I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.

NLT.2:
“I long for the years gone by
when God took care of me,
NLT.3:
when he lit up the way before me
and I walked safely through the darkness.
NLT.4:
When I was in my prime,
God’s friendship was felt in my home.
NLT.5:
The Almighty was still with me,
and my children were around me.
NLT.6:
My steps were awash in cream,
and the rocks gushed olive oil for me.
NLT.7:
“Those were the days when I went to the city gate
and took my place among the honored leaders.
NLT.8:
The young stepped aside when they saw me,
and even the aged rose in respect at my coming.
NLT.9:
The princes stood in silence
and put their hands over their mouths.
NLT.10:
The highest officials of the city stood quietly,
holding their tongues in respect.
NLT.11:
“All who heard me praised me.
All who saw me spoke well of me.
NLT.12:
For I assisted the poor in their need
and the orphans who required help.
NLT.13:
I helped those without hope, and they blessed me.
And I caused the widows’ hearts to sing for joy.
NLT.14:
Everything I did was honest.
Righteousness covered me like a robe,
and I wore justice like a turban.
NLT.15:
I served as eyes for the blind
and feet for the lame.
NLT.16:
I was a father to the poor
and assisted strangers who needed help.
NLT.17:
I broke the jaws of godless oppressors
and plucked their victims from their teeth.
NLT.18:
“I thought, ‘Surely I will die surrounded by my family
after a long, good life.
NLT.19:
For I am like a tree whose roots reach the water,
whose branches are refreshed with the dew.
NLT.20:
New honors are constantly bestowed on me,
and my strength is continually renewed.’
NLT.21:
“Everyone listened to my advice.
They were silent as they waited for me to speak.
NLT.22:
And after I spoke, they had nothing to add,
for my counsel satisfied them.
NLT.23:
They longed for me to speak as people long for rain.
They drank my words like a refreshing spring rain.
NLT.24:
When they were discouraged, I smiled at them.
My look of approval was precious to them.
NLT.25:
Like a chief, I told them what to do.
I lived like a king among his troops
and comforted those who mourned.

NET.5: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me;
NET.6: when my steps were bathed with butter and the rock poured out for me streams of olive oil!
